pr_title: unblock Unix Domain Socket on Dispose on macOS
pr_body:
fixes #101539
When. `Interop.Sys.Disconnect` is called on macOS with UDS, it fails and we end up in endless `TryUnblockSocket` loop. 

We _could_ fallback to `Shutdown` on  any error - this is just smallest change to fix the reported issue., 
Lot of the abortive jargon around here really make sense only for TCP imho and I'm n to sure how applicable the logic is to other socket types.

This  actually is `Socket` problem IMHO. It boils down to waking pending I/O on UnixDomainSocket. 
I wrote `System.Net.Sockets.Tests.UnixDomainSocketTest.UdsReceiveGetsCanceledByDispose` test (similar to we have for UDP & TCP) and it works as expected on Linux but hangs on maOC. 

tagging @tmds in case he wants to take a look. I did quick test with 6,.0 and it hangs as well

Interesting, thanks for the tip! As another workaround, we've switched to using the cancelled cancellable ReadAsync which in some ways feels better, but in others not so much (have to create an intermediate class to ReadAsync everything which might become pretty slow).

Another option would be to send some "closing" message to wake up the pending `Read`. For blocking sync IO the call is really stuck in Kernel call. But that _may_ mess up the BinaryReader. Or do non-blocking IO instead of `async` .
